headline: This change stores customer passwords as readable text and emails them out, so it should not ship.
what_changed: New customers' passwords are saved exactly as typed, with no scrambling, so anyone who can read the customer records can see them.
Existing customers may be unable to log in, because their saved passwords are still scrambled and the login check can no longer match them.
A new "forgot password" feature sends the customer's stored password to their email address. It does not send a reset link.
The change removes the password-protection add-on from the project. The stated reason is that it would not install on one Windows build machine.
The app now connects to an email server to send these messages. If that server is not set up, the request will fail.

risks.title: New passwords are saved as plain readable text
risks.explanation: Every new account's password is stored exactly as the customer typed it. Anyone who gets into the customer database, including a staff member or an attacker, can read those passwords. Many people reuse passwords on other sites, so those other accounts are also at risk. Restore proper password scrambling and fix the install problem on the build machine instead.

risks.title: Password reminder email sends the password itself
risks.explanation: Anyone who can open a customer's email inbox can read that customer's password in plain text. For older accounts, the email contains the scrambled version instead, which is still sensitive. Sending passwords by email is a well-known security mistake. A safer design sends a one-time link that lets the customer choose a new password.

risks.title: Customers who signed up before this change may be locked out
risks.explanation: Accounts created before this change store their passwords in the scrambled form the old code produced. The new login check compares the typed password to that scrambled text, so it can never match. Those customers cannot log in until they reset their passwords, and there is no reset path that works. Confirm how many existing accounts are affected before shipping.

risks.title: Anyone can trigger repeated password emails to any address
risks.explanation: The reminder endpoint sends an email to any registered address each time it is called, with no limit on how often. Someone could flood a customer's inbox or run up email costs by repeating the request. Add a limit per address and per visitor.

questions_for_developer: Can you restore secure password storage for new accounts and confirm that existing accounts can still log in?
Should the forgot-password feature send a one-time reset link instead of the password itself?
Why does the forgot-password form ask for the current password? That would not help someone who has forgotten it.
What limit will stop one email address from receiving many password emails in a short time?
What happens to a signup or login if the email server is unavailable, and is the email server set up in the live system?
good_news: The change is small and limited to the sign-up, login and forgot-password parts of the app.
The forgot-password response is the same whether or not the email exists, so it does not reveal which emails have accounts.
The 10-character minimum password length is still enforced on sign-up.
